question: The Danish mussel industry is currently facing significant challenges in the wake of the implementation of the revised Fisheries Control Regulation. According to the Danish authorities, the previous sampling scheme can no longer be used, and yet a new sampling plan – which needs to be approved by both the Danish Environmental Protection Agency and the European Commission – is not expected to be in place until 2027.
This situation is causing significant uncertainty for fishers and processing firms, with shutdowns and job losses on the cards as a result of an administrative vacuum. 1.

Was it the Commission’s intention for the implementation of the revised Fisheries Control Regulation to result in a transitional period during which the existing sampling scheme can no longer be used, and no new scheme can yet be approved and implemented?

Since some of the new control provisions were enforced only as of 10 July 2026, what is the Commission’s justification for the fact that the previous scheme cannot be maintained until a new sampling plan can enter into force?
Will the Commission bring in a temporary transitional solution or other flexible approach to allow mussel fishing to continue without unnecessary administrative obstacles?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.11.2026) Denmark did not have a Commission approved weighing derogation to allow for the sample weighing of mussel landings.

However, the existing Danish control plan for the weighing of fishery products after transport has recently been extended to the mussels fishery concerned, so that it now allows for the sample weighing of unsorted catches of mussels, after transport, to determine each quantity of each species.

Denmark may continue to apply the control plan until 10 January 2027 as per Council Regulation (EC) 1224/20091, including to the mussels fishery concerned. To be able to use a control plan after that date, Denmark can apply for a new control plan under Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/19322.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 1224/2009 of 20 November 2009 establishing a Union control system for ensuring

compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. 2 Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1932 of 10 August 2026 laying down detailed rules for the implementation of Council Regulation (EC) No 1224/2009 as regards the weighing of fishery products, their control and inspection, and the adoption of sampling plans, control plans and common control programmes.
